title: Resume/backfill protocol and SDK patch for truncated SSE sessions after gateway restart
creator: Aisha Kumari
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported truncated streaming responses (SSE) and duplicated final tokens following a rolling gateway restart on 2026-02-24. Symptom: clients observed streams that cut off mid-token or returned a duplicate final token after a transient disconnect; some SDKs surfaced this as a partial transcript and triggered downstream validation failures. Impact: several high-volume hosted customers saw user-facing truncation or corrupted chat transcripts; production SLAs and a support P1 were opened.

Root cause hypothesis: a race between the gateway's connection handoff and the session finalization path. During the restart windows some in-flight sessions had their in-memory finalization marker cleared while the per-session ephemeral checkpoints were not persisted before the socket was closed. When the client attempted to resume, the server accepted a resume but lacked the authoritative final-token anchor, producing either a truncated stream (no final flush) or replayed duplicate final tokens when a stale checkpoint reconciled with a late finalization write. The issue was exacerbated by our current resume handshake being optimistic and not exchanging a reliable per-token checkpoint (we were using a last-offset timestamp only).

Goals: 1) Stop further customer impact by introducing server-side durable session anchors that survive gateway restarts. 2) Provide a safe backfill and resume protocol that minimizes duplicate or missing tokens. 3) Patch client SDKs to detect and reconcile ambiguous final tokens with minimal UX impact. 4) Add telemetry and runbooks for fast detection and customer remediation.

Planned fixes:
- Server: implement "session-anchor" persisted in Redis (TTL 24h) that stores last_ack_token_id, last_stream_checksum, and model-config-hash. On graceful or unclean shutdown the gateway will attempt to persist atomic session anchors as part of connection draining.
- Resume handshake: extend SSE resume handshake to include client_provided_last_seen_token_id and server_anchor_token_id; server will compare and either backfill missing tokens (if deterministic re-run possible) or emit a structured "repair_hint" event instructing client on regen options.
- Backfill strategy: attempt deterministic backfill by re-running the generation with the same seed/config only for model variants that support deterministic replay; if not possible, emit repair_hint and schedule a best-effort async re-generation that customer teams can opt into.
- SDK: detect duplicate final tokens using token-level IDs and dedupe final sentinel; transparently merge partial transcript segments and expose a "repaired" flag on the response object. Add client-side exponential resume backoff and a small reconciliation API endpoint to request server-side backfill.
- Observability: add metrics (anchor_persist_failures, resume_mismatch_rate, backfill_success_rate) and an alert targeting >0.1% resume_mismatch_rate per deployment.
- Runbook & comms: author incident playbook, templated customer communication, and support-side checklist for manual backfills.

Trade-offs & constraints: durable anchors add a small write to Redis per active session which increases host I/O; we mitigate with batching and aggressive TTL. Deterministic replays are only possible for a subset of models; for non-deterministic models we accept a best-effort repair_hint approach to avoid reintroducing inconsistent outputs. SDK changes are non-breaking; however, older SDKs will not dedupe, so we include a server-side compatibility shim to avoid delivering duplicate final tokens when possible.

Success criteria: deploy to canary with tracing enabled, observe resume_mismatch_rate < 0.01% in canary for 48 hours, and then roll to prod. No new customer escalations for truncated streams after full rollout.
comments: 2026-02-26 - initial triage by SRE and oncall: confirmed customer traces showing socket FIN from gateway immediately followed by attach from edge with no finalization event. Assigned to ENG-200849.

2026-02-27 - architecture sync (Aisha, Miguel, Priya, SRE): agreed to implement session-anchor in Redis and extend resume handshake; noted write amplification concerns and settled on 250ms batching window for anchors.
2026-03-01 - PR opened: runtime PR #1378 implements anchor writes, resume handshake validation, and a lightweight backfill controller. Linked above.

2026-03-02 - SDK PR for JS and Python (WIP): add token-id dedupe and repaired flag. PM and DX reviewed; requested clearer API surface for repaired boolean. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/422

2026-03-03 - QA notes: deterministic backfill validated on distilled-small and r-infer-1; non-deterministic models produce repair_hint as expected. Load test shows Redis anchor write adds 2% p99 latency for active sessions; within acceptable threshold for canary. Details in confluence link.

2026-03-04 - Canary rollout: deployed runtime-1.20 canary to us-east-1 (10% traffic) with tracing and alerts. Initial telemetry: resume_mismatch_rate reduced from 0.45% to 0.02% in canary. Observed 3 customers requesting manual backfill; support executed playbook and confirmed repaired transcripts.

2026-03-05 - Engineering review: code-first approach approved, prepare staged prod rollout. Need to confirm Dedicated/private compatibility (ensure Redis anchor dependency can be configured to customer-hosted stores for Private deployments). Action: add config knobs and document in private-deploy guide.
Design feedback (2026-03-02): UX: present repaired flag with human-friendly reason; avoid auto-surfacing raw token IDs to users. Action for DX: create migration guide for app teams.
Next steps: finish SDK PRs, add Dedicated/Private config for anchor store, complete security review exemption checklist, ramp canary to 50% and close ticket after 1 week of stable telemetry.
